Class GameScene

java.lang.Object
it.polimi.ingsw.am02.client.view.gui.scenes.GameScene
public class GameScene extends Object
The main game scene of the GUI. This class handles the rendering of the game board, player hands, sidebar, and animations for various game events.

    • snapshot

      public static GameScene.SceneState snapshot(GameModel model)
      Captures an immutable snapshot of the given model. Safe to call from any thread (see GameScene.SceneState). Callers that observe events on the network thread should snapshot here, in event order, and pass the result to render(SceneState) on the FX thread.
      Parameters:
      model - the model to snapshot
      Returns:
      a frozen view of the model's current state

    • setModel

      public void setModel(GameModel model)
      Binds the live GameModel to this scene without triggering a render.

      Rendering uses immutable GameScene.SceneState snapshots, but a few helpers (the turn-order cave, the card-taken/totem animations) still read the live model for stable, session-constant data such as totem colours and the local nickname. When the scene is created lazily on a setup/phase event we build it without an auto-refresh and bind the model here, so those helpers have a non-null reference before the first render(SceneState).

      Parameters:
      model - the live game model for this session

    • render

      public void render(GameScene.SceneState snapshot)
      Renders a previously captured GameScene.SceneState.

      Must be called on the JavaFX application thread. It mutates FX-thread-only state (lastState, viewedPlayerHand, the animation queue) and schedules the actual node updates, so that the FX thread remains the single thread that ever touches the GUI.

      Parameters:
      snapshot - the frozen state to render

    • showNewEraAnimation

      public void showNewEraAnimation(GameScene.SceneState snapshot, Era newEra, List<String> u, List<String> l)
      Displays an animation for the beginning of a new era.

      Must be called on the JavaFX application thread. The board is refreshed from the supplied (event-ordered) snapshot and the era overlay is appended right after it in the same animation queue, so the "ERA n" banner plays in lockstep with the board frame that introduced the new era — even while a reconnection history is being replayed.

      Parameters:
      snapshot - the frozen state captured when the era-change event arrived.
      newEra - The new era.
      u - New upper row buildings.
      l - New lower row buildings.

    • enqueueForfeitBanner

      public void enqueueForfeitBanner(long seconds)
      Queues the forfeit banner into the animation FIFO. Must be called on the FX thread.

      The banner is intentionally routed through the same animationQueue as every other on-screen step rather than shown immediately: the server fires the global-timer notification at the end of a reconnection replay, so if the banner were raised on its own Platform.runLater it would jump the fast FX-pulse queue and appear before the still-draining visual replay (the infamous "120s shown first"). Enqueuing it guarantees it surfaces only after everything queued ahead of it has played out.

      Parameters:
      seconds - the forfeit countdown value supplied by the server

    • enqueueDismissForfeitBanner

      public void enqueueDismissForfeitBanner()
      Queues the dismissal of the forfeit banner into the animation FIFO. Must be called on the FX thread. Routed through the queue for the same reason as enqueueForfeitBanner(long) and, crucially, so the dismissal can never overtake a still-queued show (which would leave the banner stuck on screen).
